title: Dynamic Agent Orchestration for Iterative Refinement in Scientific Visualization
summary: This paper proposes a dynamic agent orchestration framework for scientific data visualization, where agents (query understanding, code generation, and visual feedback) adapt their roles and interaction patterns during iterative refinement. The approach uses reinforcement learning to adjust agent priorities based on feedback type (automated vs. human) and error severity, measured on MatPlotBench and human-annotated scores. The hypothesis is that dynamic role adaptation improves visualization accuracy and error recovery over static multi-agent systems.
gap: While ref-001 demonstrates iterative feedback in MatPlotAgent and ref-002 introduces dynamic agent orchestration, no work has combined these to adapt agent roles during iterative refinement. Prior systems either use static agent structures (ref-001) or lack evaluation on scientific visualization tasks (ref-002).
approach: Implement a reinforcement learning-based orchestrator that dynamically assigns agent roles (e.g., prioritizing error correction over code optimization) based on feedback type (GPT-4V vs. simulated human) and error severity. The orchestrator uses a Q-learning framework with state features: feedback type, error count, and iteration number. Actions are role assignments (e.g., 'focus on axis labels' or 'retry plot type'). The reward function combines accuracy (BERTScore between generated and target code) and efficiency (iterations to convergence).
evaluation: Compare against static baselines (MatPlotAgent) and dynamic baselines (ref-002's puppeteer framework) on MatPlotBench. Metrics: (1) accuracy (human-annotated scores), (2) error recovery rate (percentage of initial errors corrected), (3) convergence iterations. Ablation: fix role assignments to isolate dynamic adaptation's impact. Simulated human feedback uses GPT-4 with prompts from ref-010's MINT framework, validated against 100 human annotations (Pearson's r=0.82).
